note: Track intervals, step 6: the 7ths and the tritone, then all twelve intervals up, then down. The first game narrows to the three new intervals with "set" and names each answer as its button shows it with the plain word beside it; the next two are set to "level": "advanced" and change one thing each (all twelve, then the direction). One extra line per block: a feel, what to do when two answers sound alike, what stays the same going down.

exercise.title: The 7ths, the tritone, then all twelve
exercise.why: The two 7ths and the tritone are told apart by how far the upper note stops under the octave, so listening for that gap names all three.

cells.text:
Press Start in the game below: it plays two notes, one after the other. Pick m7 for a minor 7th, M7 for a major 7th or TT for the tritone.
Practice until you hear where the upper note stops before you pick: just under the octave, a step under it, or halfway up.

Press Start in the game below: now any of the twelve intervals can come.
If two answers sound alike, press Replay above the answers and listen to how far the upper note is from the lower one, not to the notes themselves.

Press Start in the game below: the same twelve intervals, with the upper note first and the lower one after it.
When you change the direction, the notes come in a new order but the distance between them is the same.
